sentences.text: The genus Craspedodon contains only one known species, Craspedodon lonzeensis, which is recognized solely from three teeth discovered in Belgium.
These fossils were identified because they displayed anatomical similarities to the teeth of Iguanodon.
The holotype specimen, defined as the specific specimen the species is based on, IRSNB R59, is the smallest of the three recovered teeth.
This animal lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Santonian stage in what is now Europe.
Belgian paleontologist Louis Dollo described the herbivorous dinosaur Craspedodon lonzeensis in 1883 from fossils found in the Lonzée Member.
The geological age of the Lonzée Member is now understood to span the Coniacian to Santonian stages, corresponding to a time range estimated from 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago.
It is believed Craspedodon arrived in Europe via land bridges connecting the continent to Asia during the Aptian period, rather than from North America.
Craspedodon was originally classified as an ornithopod related to Iguanodon, but the Paleobi Database currently lists its parent group as Iguanodontoidea.
A 2007 study suggested the tooth shape, ridge length, and thickened base might indicate membership in Neoceratopsia, specifically basal Ceratopsoidea.

Researchers were unable to determine if Craspedodon is a valid diagnostic taxon or a nomen dubium because tooth anatomy is too poorly understood, leading some to suggest it might instead represent a hadrosauroid ornithopod.
